newsitem.title: USA: Komag sees losses at AKCL unit.
newsitem.headline: Komag sees losses at AKCL unit.

text.p: Komag Inc said Thursday it expects losses at its 50 percent-owned Japanese subsidiary Asahi Komag Co Ltd (AKCL) to continue for the next two quarters.
"We now believe that AKCL's equity contribution to Komag will continue to remain negative for the next two quarters," said Stephen Johnson, president and chief executive in a statement.
AKCL reported a loss for the second quarter that reduced Komag's overall earnings per share by about $0.02 due to a transition to magnetoresistive disk products.
Komag reported second quarter profits of $11.7 million, or $0.22 a share, compared to $42.6 million, or $0.80 a share, in the comparable year-ago quarter.
Komag reiterated earnings per share in the third and fourth quarter will be below first and second quarter levels.
In order to cut expenses Komag said it plans to cut current quarterly capital expenditures by 40 percent to 50 percent from current levels of about $70 million.

Komag said it will focus expenditures on projects that improve process capabilities and support an increasing magnetoresistive product mix. The company will also curtail production capacity expansion and may take other appropriate cost cutting measures.

"Our near-term financial recovery is currently difficult to predict and depends upon resumed growth of end-user demand for enterprise-class disk drives, the recapture of lost order volume, improved manufacturing efficiencies, and the timing of new product qualifications," Johnson said.

Komag, which makes components for computer disk drives, said its second quarter results were hurt by a slowdown in market demand for high-end disk drive products, lower factory utilization due to changing customer orders, yield-related production issues late in the quarter, and increased reserves related to inventory.
